en: I worship Him who dwells on the mountain, who is an ocean of the nectar of compassion, who is the supreme one intent on the hunt, and who is most beautiful,
the range of all moving and non-moving beings.
I take refuge in the Lord, the son of Hari and Hara. || 1 ||
He who fulfills the thoughts of the multitude of those prostrate before him; the primordial teacher to whom the gods bow; the artisan of the deities;
he who is delighted by the sacred syllable *praṇava* and possesses a beautiful couch.
I take refuge in the Lord, the son of Hari and Hara. || 2 ||
Holding a lotus, a conch, a mace, and a club;
bearing a bludgeon, a hammer, an arrow, and a bow;
with hands shimmering with a dagger, a lance, and a spear.
I take refuge in the Lord, the son of Hari and Hara. || 3 ||
To him whose mind is a stainless lake, who is the sun,
who holds a broad cane, who bestows great fame,
and who wields a fierce bow for the shattering of adversaries.
I take refuge in the Lord, the son of Hari and Hara. || 4 ||
The sandals honored by the entire world, which bring joy to virtuous devotees upon a single worship,
and which initiate the protection of those with meritorious devotion.
I take refuge in the Lord, the son of Hari and Hara. || 5 ||
He whose glory is proclaimed as a refuge, who is devoted to His bhaktas, who is the elixir of the self for those who wear His feet like water-vessels,
and whose ornaments are the sacred ashes held in His excellent hands.
I take refuge in the Lord, the son of Hari and Hara. || 6 ||
Marked with musk and radiant with the tilaka-ornament, frequented by herds of deer yet agitated by the hunt,
it possesses the wondrous appearance of the seat of the Best of Deer.
I take refuge in the Lord, the son of Hari and Hara. || 7 ||
The most excellent Guru, whose eyes are the nectar of compassion, who is peerless and the liberator from all maladies,
who bestows supreme happiness and reveals the Self.
I take refuge in the Lord, the son of Hari and Hara. || 8 ||
The eightfold basis is complete.
